findings.title: cook_method migration default misclassifies all posts as raw_html
findings.body: The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` sets a default of 1 for every existing post (and every new post that does not explicitly assign cook_method). In `app/models/post.rb`, `Post.cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. With the conventional 0-indexed enum used elsewhere in this file (`Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`, `Enum.new(:flag_threshold_reached, ...)`), `:regular` is 0 and `:raw_html` is 1. The default therefore marks every existing post as raw_html, which combined with the new `Post#cook` behavior (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) and the `before_save` callback `self.cooked = cook(raw, topic_id: topic_id) unless new_record?`, means that the next save of any existing post overwrites the previously rendered `cooked` HTML with raw markdown. New posts created via `PostCreator` without an explicit `:cook_method` opts become raw_html too, because `setup_post` only assigns the value when `@opts[:cook_method].present?`. The migration default should be 0 (or whatever value corresponds to `:regular`).

findings.title: External content rendered as raw HTML in embed iframe
findings.body: `raw post.cooked` renders the stored `cooked` value without HTML escaping. Posts created via `TopicEmbed.import` are stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, which causes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim. The `raw` value originates from RSS feed items (`SimpleRSS`) or the unfiltered output of `Readability::Document.new(...).content` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which can contain arbitrary HTML, including `<script>` and event handlers. When that post is shown in the embed iframe hosted on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the malicious markup executes in the Discourse origin. Either sanitize `doc.content` (and the RSS content) before storing, or run `cooked` through the discourse sanitizer pipeline regardless of `cook_method` for the embed view. The current combination is a stored XSS that is reachable by anyone able to publish a feed entry or scrape a hostile page.

findings.title: JavaScript injection via request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` inserts the raw `Referer` header value into a JavaScript string literal inside a `<script>` tag. HTML ERB escaping does not apply within script blocks, so any `'` or `</script>` in the referer can break out of the string. An attacker controlling a page on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (which passes the host check in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`) can navigate to the embed URL with a Referer like `http://embeddable_host/x');malicious_code;//'` — that referer is a syntactically valid URL whose host still matches `embeddable_host`, so it satisfies the controller's check, and its path is then injected into the script. Use `j request.referer.to_s %>` (or `escape_javascript`) to JSON-encode/escape the value into the script, or read `document.referrer` in JS instead.

findings.title: Race window between lookup and create in TopicEmbed.import
findings.body: Two workers can both observe `embed.blank?` and enter the `Topic.transaction` branch simultaneously. The unique index on `embed_url` will cause one of the `TopicEmbed.create!` calls to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued here and will propagate out of the transaction, leaving the other worker's topic orphaned from the embed row (or vice versa). The `post.blank?` branch also still falls through to `post` without ensuring the embed row exists for the new topic. Wrap the `create!` in a rescue that re-fetches the embed (or upsert) so concurrent importers converge on a single TopicEmbed record.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on RSS items with nil content/title
findings.body: Inside the loop, `i.content.scrub` and `i.title` are used unconditionally. Many real-world feeds omit `content` and/or `title` on items, which raises `NoMethodError` (nil.scrub) and aborts the rest of the poll. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure is logged and silently dropped each hour, so a single bad feed item stops all later items from being imported. Add nil guards for `i.content` and `i.title`, and wrap the parse/iteration in a rescue so one malformed item doesn't poison the whole run.

findings.title: Multiple fetches can race past existing-embed guard
findings.body: `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` followed by `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` followed by another `exists?` check then `fetch_http` is not atomic. Two workers can both pass the first check and then both run `PollFeed` (which itself iterates the entire feed) and `import_remote` for the same URL, producing duplicate topics for the same source. The 60-second Redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?` only protects a single user — jobs queued by different users, or staff with `no_throttle: true`, do not serialize. Either short-circuit with a Redis lock around the full `perform_retrieve` block, or make `TopicEmbed.import` idempotent (lookup-or-insert) and rely on the unique index.

findings.title: Unbounded fetch from arbitrary URLs in import_remote
findings.body: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` has no timeout and no size cap. `Kernel#open` (open-uri) will happily read an arbitrarily large response body into memory before Readability parses it. An attacker serving huge `text/html` from a page on `embeddable_host` can use the embed pipeline to make Discourse allocate large amounts of memory (and occupy a worker for a long time) simply by triggering `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` from a controlled page. Pass `read_timeout`, `open_timeout`, and/or a content-length limit to `open` (e.g. `URI.parse(url).open(read_timeout: 5, open_timeout: 5) { |io| io.read(2.megabytes) }`).

findings.title: Stray require_dependency 'email/sender'
findings.body: The job requires `email/sender`, but the body of `execute` only uses `TopicRetriever` and `User`. The require is dead code that will load and initialize the email-sender module on every job execution (including during tests). It also misleads future maintainers about the job's responsibilities. Remove it.

findings.title: Missing test for invalid-referer failure and XSS-vulnerable layout interaction
findings.body: The spec covers missing host, no embed_url, and a successful happy-path, but it never exercises the `URI(request.referer).host` comparison with a referer that has the right host but a hostile payload (the case that enables the script-injection finding in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`). It also doesn't verify that a referer whose host doesn't match `embeddable_host` is rejected. Add tests for both: a referer on a different host (expect non-success) and an assertion that any unsafe characters in the referer are not echoed verbatim into the response body (e.g. `expect(response.body).not_to include(request.referer)` or assert that the postMessage target is JSON-escaped).
